hook.line: Both phrases are about not reacting, but one is innocent and one is not. Mix them up in an essay and you accuse someone of wrongdoing, or let them off.

examples.es: Don Hernando vio el error y hizo la vista gorda.
examples.en: Don Hernando saw the mistake and turned a blind eye.

examples.es: Tomás no vio el error: lo pasó por alto.
examples.en: Tomás didn't see the mistake: he overlooked it.

examples.es: Hice la vista gorda porque era mi amigo.
examples.en: I turned a blind eye because he was my friend.

examples.es: Mariana pasó por alto la fecha.
La policía pasó por alto una pista.

rule:
Ask one question: did the person see it?

*Hacer la vista gorda* means yes: they saw something wrong and pretended not to. It is a choice, and it carries blame: *Don Hernando vio el error y hizo la vista gorda*.

*Pasar por alto* is neutral. It can mean they missed it by accident, or that they skipped it as unimportant. No blame: *Mariana pasó por alto la fecha*.

English "overlook" covers both, which is why this is easy to mix up. Spanish splits it.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a near-synonym contrast: two expressions that overlap in English but differ in intent.

readAndPick.es: Don Hernando vio el error y hizo la vista gorda.
options: Don Hernando overlooked the mistake by accident.
Don Hernando saw the mistake and turned a blind eye.
Don Hernando fixed the mistake.

readAndPick.es: Tomás no vio el error: lo pasó por alto.
options: Tomás overlooked the mistake without seeing it.
Tomás turned a blind eye to the mistake.
Tomás corrected the mistake.

readAndPick.es: Hice la vista gorda porque era mi amigo.
options: I overlooked it by accident because he was my friend.
I turned a blind eye because he was my friend.
I told on him because he was my friend.

readAndPick.es: Mariana pasó por alto la fecha.
options: Mariana overlooked the date.
Mariana turned a blind eye to the date.
Mariana remembered the date.
He overlooked it.
He turned a blind eye.
He saw nothing.

readAndPick.es: La policía pasó por alto una pista.
options: The police turned a blind eye to a clue.
The police found a clue.
The police overlooked a clue.

readAndPick.es: Vale hizo la vista gorda con el cliente que no pagó.
options: Vale turned a blind eye to the customer who didn't pay.
Vale didn't notice the customer who didn't pay.
Vale overlooked the customer who paid.
He overlooked the figure.
He turned a blind eye to the figure.
He gave the figure.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Tomás no vio el error: lo ___.* (*pasó por alto* or *hizo la vista gorda*) Tomás didn't see the mistake: he overlooked it.
yourTurn.answer: Tomás no vio el error: lo pasó por alto.
yourTurn.why: He did not see it, so there is nothing to pretend about.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Don Hernando vio el error y ___.* (*pasó por alto* or *hizo la vista gorda*) Don Hernando saw the mistake and turned a blind eye.
yourTurn.answer: Don Hernando vio el error y hizo la vista gorda.
yourTurn.why: He saw it and chose to say nothing, which is a blind eye.

yourTurn.answer: Mariana pasó por alto la fecha.
yourTurn.why: A simple miss, with no blame: *pasar por alto*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I turned a blind eye because he was my friend.
yourTurn.answer: Hice la vista gorda porque era mi amigo.
yourTurn.why: A choice made knowingly: *hacer la vista gorda*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The police overlooked a clue.
yourTurn.answer: La policía pasó por alto una pista.
yourTurn.why: They did not notice or value it, so *pasar por alto*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say about Vale: She turned a blind eye to the customer who didn't pay.
yourTurn.answer: Vale hizo la vista gorda con el cliente que no pagó.
accept: Vale hizo la vista gorda con la cliente que no pagó.
Vale hizo la vista gorda ante el cliente que no pagó.
yourTurn.why: She saw it and let it go on purpose, so *hacer la vista gorda*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a mistake with no blame: *Hizo la vista gorda ante el precio.* (use *pasó por alto*)
yourTurn.why: Without blame, *pasar por alto* takes the noun directly.

pitfalls.wrong: Don Hernando pasó por alto el error y no dijo nada, porque quería protegerlo.
pitfalls.right: Don Hernando hizo la vista gorda ante el error.
pitfalls.why: Almost. If he saw it and kept quiet on purpose, Spanish uses *hacer la vista gorda*.

pitfalls.wrong: Hizo la vista gorda el dato.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Hacer la vista gorda* is about wrongdoing; a missed figure is *pasar por alto*.

pitfalls.wrong: Pasó por alto ante el error.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Ante* belongs to *hacer la vista gorda*; *pasar por alto* takes the noun directly.

personal: Think of a time you missed something, and a time you chose not to react. Say each with the right phrase.
